Rashi on Shabbat 5a:10:1.hebrew: שלשל - השפיל, כמו היה משלשל בחבל:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:10:1.english: [He] lowered - [That is,] he lowered [it], as in: "He was lowering with a rope."

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:10:2.english: Below three [handbreadths] - For it is [considered] like the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:11:1.hebrew: והא עומד קתני - העני עומד בחוץ, והא יושב הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:11:1.english: And doesn't [the mishna] teach "standing"? - [The mishna states:] "The poor person stands outside" — yet behold, he is sitting!

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:11:2.english: [Where he is] stooping - He bends himself [over].

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:11:3.english: And if you wish, say - [It refers to a case] where he is standing in a pit, and his hand is close to its edge.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:12:1.hebrew: איכפל תנא כו' - טרח התנא בכל זאת, ולא היה לו להודיענו דמוציא מרשות לרשות חייב אלא על ידי דברים הללו שאין דרכן בכך? לתני: פשט כנף בגדו לפנים, דהוי ד':
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:12:1.english: Did the Tanna go to the trouble, etc. - Did the Tanna go to all this trouble, and could he not have informed us that one who carries out from [one] domain to [another] domain is liable, except through these things that are not the usual manner? Let him teach: "He extended the corner of his garment inside," which is four [handbreadths]!

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:13:1.hebrew: היכא דאחשבה - זה העושה מלאכה נתכוון לתתה ליד חבירו, כי מתניתין:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:13:1.english: Where he deemed it significant - This one who performs the labor intended to place it into his fellow's hand, as in our Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:13:2.hebrew: אבל היכא דלא אחשבה - שהלכה ונחה מעצמה ביד חבירו, דהאי דזריק לא אחשבה ליד חבירו לאנוחה בגווה, דלא נתכוון לכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:13:2.english: However, where he did not deem it significant - Where it went and came to rest on its own in the hand of his fellow, for the one who threw [it] did not deem the hand of his fellow significant to set [it] down inside it, as he did not intend for this.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:14:1.english: [He] stood - The recipient [stood] in his place and received [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:14:2.english: [He is] liable - The thrower [is liable].

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:14:3.english: Exempt - The thrower [is exempt], as he did not perform [the act of] placing.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:16:1.hebrew: מאי קמיבעיא ליה - מאי ספיקא איכא? מאיזה טעמא יפטור? הא עבד עקירה והנחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:16:1.english: What is his dilemma - What doubt is there? For what reason would he be exempt? Behold, he performed [both] an uprooting and a placing.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:16:2.hebrew: כשני בני אדם דמיא ופטור - דהוו להו שנים שעשאוה, דכיון שלא הניח החפץ לילך עד מקום הילוכו ולנוח, אלא רץ אחריו ועכבו — הויא ליה עקירה קמייתא בלא הנחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:16:2.english: [They] are considered like two people, and [he is] exempt - For they are [considered like] two [people] who performed it [together]; since he did not let the object travel to the end of its course and come to rest, but rather ran after it and intercepted it, the first uprooting is [left] without a placement.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:17:1.hebrew: מה לי הטעינו חבירו - דפטר ליה תנא דמתניתין, דקתני: או שנתן לתוכה והוציא — שניהן פטורין:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:17:1.english: What is [the difference] to me if his fellow loaded him - For the Tanna of our Mishnah exempts him, as it teaches: "Or [if the homeowner] placed [it] into [his hand] and [the poor person] carried [it] out, both of them are exempt."

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:17:2.hebrew: לא תימא קיבל - פשט ידו וירדו לתוכה, דלא עבד מעשה:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:17:2.english: Do not say: He received - [Meaning that] he extended his hand and [the rainwater] fell into it, for he did not perform an action.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:17:3.hebrew: אלא אימא קלט - השתא סלקא דעתך: כשהיה הקילוח יורד, הכה בידו אחת וקבלו בחברתה, דעבד ליה עקירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:17:3.english: Rather, say: He caught [it] - Now you might think: When the stream was descending, he struck [it] with one hand and caught it in the other [hand], for he performed an act of lifting for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:1:1.english: Roofed - That it has a roof.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:1:2.hebrew: כמאן דמלי - דבר סתום מכל צד הוי כמלא חפצים עד גגו, דאין אוירו חשיב אויר. הלכך, כל הנזרק לתוכו הוי כמונח:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:1:2.english: As one that is full - Something enclosed on all sides is considered as [though] filled with objects up to its roof, for its airspace is not considered [mere] airspace. Therefore, anything thrown into it is considered as [if it has] come to rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:2:1.hebrew: התינח רה"י - דבע"ה, אלא רשות הרבים דעני, מי מוקמת ליה במקורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:2:1.english: Granted, the private domain - [That is,] that of the homeowner; but the public domain of the poor man, can you establish it as covered?

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:2:2.hebrew: לדגלי מדבר - וכל מלאכות דבשבת ממשכן גמרי לקמן, מדנסמכה פרשת שבת לפרשת משכן בויקהל:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:2:2.english: To the banners of the wilderness - And all the labors of Shabbat we derive from the Mishkan [Tabernacle] later on, since the passage of Shabbat was juxtaposed to the passage of the Mishkan in [Parashat] Vayakhel.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:1.hebrew: הא מני - דלא בעי מקום ד', אחרים היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:1.english: Whose is this - [This mishnah,] which does not require an area of four [handbreadths], is [the view of] Aḥerim.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:2.hebrew: עמד במקומו - זרק חפץ וקבלו אחר, עמד המקבל במקומו וקבל:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:2.english: [He] stood in his place - [Where one] threw an object and another received it, [and] the recipient stood in his place and received [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:3.hebrew: חייב - הזורק, דאיהו עבד עקירה והנחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:3.english: [He is] liable - [It is] the thrower, for he performed [both] the lifting and the placing.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:4.english: [He] moved - The recipient [moved] from his place and ran toward the object and received it.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:5.hebrew: פטור - הזורק, דלא איתעביד הנחה מכחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:3:5.english: [He is] exempt - [This refers to] the thrower, because the placement was not effected by his force.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:4:1.english: That he spread the corners of his garment - He spread out his garment, so that it is [an area of] four [handbreadths].

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:6:1.english: It is a private domain - And why is he liable for carrying out?

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:7:1.hebrew: לימא - מתניתין דלא חשיב ליה רה"י, דלא כרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:7:1.english: Shall we say - [That] our mishnah, which does not consider it a private domain, is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:7:2.english: And threw - From the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:7:3.hebrew: ונח על גביו חייב - דאע"ג דלמטה לא הוי קנה רחב ד', הואיל ובראשו ארבע, אמרינן גוד אחית מחיצה, והוי רה"י גמור:
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:7:3.english: And it landed upon it, [he is] liable - For even though below the reed is not four [handbreadths] wide, since at its top [it is] four [handbreadths wide], we say: "Extend and lower the partition" [gud aḥit meḥitza], and it is a full-fledged private domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 5a:9:1.hebrew: למעלה מי' - הוי רה"י, הואיל ורחב ד':
Rashi on Shabbat 5a:9:1.english: Above ten [handbreadths] - It is a private domain, since it is four [handbreadths] wide.

Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:10:1.hebrew: כגון ששלשל ידו למטה מג' וקבלה - וקסבר רבי אבהו דאגד יד שמיה אגד; דאי לא הוי שמיה אגד, מאי איריא דנטל עני מתוכה? אפילו נתן בעה"ב לתוכה יהא חייב העני כשהוציא, כיון דיד העני מיירי נמי דהוה למטה מג' — דמסתמא יד בעה"ב ויד עני איירי בענין אחד, דהא כי נטל מתוך ידו של בעה"ב דהוי למטה מג', הויא יד עני נמי למטה מג' — ובכהאי גוונא, אפילו נותן בעה"ב לתוך יד העני יהא חייב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:10:1.english: "Such as where he lowered his hand below three [handbreadths] and received it" - And Rabbi Abbahu maintains that the attachment of a hand [to the body] is considered an attachment; for if it were not considered an attachment, why specifically [did the Mishnah teach the case where] the poor person took [the object] from within it [the homeowner's hand]? Even [if] the homeowner placed [it] into it [the poor person's hand], the poor person should be liable when he carried [it] out, since the poor person's hand is also dealing with [a case where] it was below three [handbreadths from the ground] — for presumably the homeowner's hand and the poor person's hand are dealing with one and the same circumstance, for when he took [it] from within the homeowner's hand, which was below three [handbreadths], the poor person's hand was also below three [handbreadths] — and in such a case, even [if] the homeowner places [the object] into the poor person's hand, [the poor person] should be liable.

Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:11:1.hebrew: בגומא - צריך לפרש בגומא שהיא רשות הרבים, כגון שרבים משתמשים בה למ"ד "תשמיש על ידי הדחק שמיה תשמיש" (לקמן שבת ד' ח:), או בענין שמהלכים שם רבים. אבל גומא שהיתה כרמלית או מקום פטור — כיון שגופו שם, ידו שהיא פשוטה לרשות הרבים לא הויא כרה"ר, דבתר גופו גריר, אע"פ שהיא למטה מג', כיון דסבר "אגד יד שמיה אגד", כדפי':
Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:11:1.english: In a hole - One must explain [that it refers to] a hole that is a public domain, such as where the public makes use of it, according to the one who holds [that] "usage under difficult conditions is considered usage" (below, Shabbat 8b), or in a manner where the public walks through it. But if the hole were a karmelit or an exempt domain — since his body is there, his hand that is outstretched into the public domain would not be [treated] like the public domain, for it is drawn after his body, even though it is below three [handbreadths from the ground], since [Rabbi Abbahu] holds [that] the attachment of a hand is considered an [effective] attachment, as [we] explained.

Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:13:1.hebrew: ה"מ היכא דאחשבא לידיה - וא"ת: ולימא הך, ולא ההיא דלעיל? וי"ל: דה"א דוקא לענין הנחה חשובה כד' על ד', אבל לגבי עקירה — לא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:13:1.english: This applies where he deemed his hand significant - And if you say: Let [Rabbi Yochanan] state this [ruling], and not that earlier one? And one can say: For [otherwise] I would have said that specifically regarding placing, [a hand] is considered like [an area of] four by four [handbreadths], but regarding lifting, it is not.

Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:16:1.hebrew: כשני בני אדם דמי ופטור - פי': כי היכי דבשני בני אדם פטור הראשון, משום דלא עבד כלל הנחה — ה"נ, כיון שחטפו מהילוכו ולא הניח החפץ ללכת עד מקום הילוכו, לא הויא הנחה, דלא נח מכח הזורק. או דילמא כאדם אחד דמי, וכיון דעביד עקירה והנחה חייב, ולא דמי לשנים שעשאוה. ור"ח גריס איפכא: "כשני בני אדם דמי וחייב" — דאמר לעיל: עמד במקומו וקבל חייב, וה"נ, כי קבלה הוא עצמו ולא חטפה מהילוכו, ליחייב, דהא איתעביד מחשבתו; או דילמא כאדם אחד דמי ופטור — דהוי כמו שנותן מימינו לשמאלו, דאע"פ שהעבירה ד' אמות פטור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:16:1.english: "They are considered like two people, and he is exempt" - Explanation: Just as in [the case of] two people, the first is exempt because he did not perform placement at all, so too here, since he snatched it from its trajectory and did not allow the object to travel to its destination, it is not [considered] a placement, as it did not come to rest by the force of the thrower. Or perhaps they are considered like one person, and since he performed [both] lifting and placement, he is liable, and it is not similar to two who performed it [together]. And Rabbeinu Chananel read the reverse: "They are considered like two people, and he is liable" — for [the Gemara] said above: "If [one] stood in his place and caught [it], [the thrower] is liable"; and so too here, when he caught it himself and did not snatch it from its trajectory, let him be liable, for his intention was fulfilled! Or perhaps they are considered like one person, and he is exempt — for it is like one who transfers [an object] from his right [hand] to his left [hand], who, even though he transported it four cubits, is exempt.

Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:1:1.hebrew: לא מחייב ר' אלא ברשות היחיד מקורה - נראה לרשב"א, דמשמע ליה מדלא נקט "מרשות היחיד לרה"י ורשות הרבים באמצע", כמו בפלוגתא דר"ע ורבנן. וההיא דגיטין, פ' הזורק (גיטין ד' עט. ושם), גבי "היתה עומדת על ראש הגג וזרקו לה" כו', וקאמר: "כמאן? כרבי, דאמר קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא" — לא סברי דרב ושמואל דהכא, דאמרי דלא חייב ר' אלא ברשות היחיד מקורה; ולדידהו, צריך לשנויי דהתם משום אינטורי, כדמשני התם אליבא דרבנן: "אפילו תימא רבנן, כי פליגי רבנן לענין שבת, אבל הכא משום אינטורי" כו':
Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:1:1.english: "Rabbi only deems [one] liable in a covered private domain" - It appears to the Rashba that [Rav and Shmuel] inferred this from the fact that [the baraita] did not formulate [the case as]: "From a private domain to a private domain with a public domain in the middle," as in the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis. And as for that [sugya] in Gittin, chapter HaZorek (Gittin 79a and there), regarding [the Mishnah]: "If she was standing on top of the roof and he threw it to her, etc.," where [the Gemara] asks: "In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi, who said: [An object] caught in the air is considered as if it came to rest?" — [the Amoraim there] do not hold like Rav and Shmuel here, who say that Rabbi only deemed [one] liable in a covered private domain. And according to them [Rav and Shmuel], one must explain that there it is because [the bill of divorce] is secured, just as [the Gemara] resolves there according to the Rabbis: "You may even say [it is in accordance with] the Rabbis; when the Rabbis disagree, [it is] with regard to Shabbat, but here [it is] because it is secured, etc."

Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:8:1.hebrew: אמאי חייב מרה"י לרה"י קא מפיק - ואפילו משום מושיט, ובדיוטא אחת, לא מחייב — לפי הירושלמי דמצריך שיקבלנו שני מידו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:8:1.english: Why is he liable? He is carrying out from a private domain to a private domain - And even on account of passing [an object] (moshit), and [even] on the same level (bediota achat), he is not liable — according to the Yerushalmi, which requires that a second [person] receive it from his hand.

Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:9:1.hebrew: כאן למטה מי' - וא"ת: נהי דרשות היחיד לא הוי, ר"ה נמי לא הוי, אלא ככרמלית, כמו עמוד גבוה שלשה ורחב ד' — ואמאי חייב? ויש לומר: דאין כרמלית בכלים, כמו שפירש רש"י לקמן גבי "היתה קופתו מונחת" כו'. קשה לר"י: מה עלה על דעתו של המקשן? דע"כ ידע דמתניתין מיירי למטה מי' בלא פירכא דר' יוסי בר' יהודה, דכל למעלה מי' הוי מקום פטור ולא מחייב לכ"ע; וא"כ, מאי פריך מרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה? הא מילתא דפשיטא היא דלמטה מי' לא הוה רה"י, דהא תנן לקמן בהזורק (לקמן שבת ד' צט.): "חולית הבור והסלע שהם גבוהים י' ורחבים ד', הנוטל מהן והנותן על גבן חייב; פחות מכן פטור". ופשיטא דרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה לא איירי אלא למעלה מי':
Tosafot on Shabbat 5a:9:1.english: Here, [it is] below ten [handbreadths] - And if you say: Granted that it is not a private domain [reshut hayachid], it is not a public domain [reshut harabim] either, but rather like a karmelit, like a pillar three [handbreadths] high and four [handbreadths] wide — and why [then] is he liable? And one can say that there is no [status of] karmelit for vessels, as Rashi explained below regarding "If his basket was placed...", etc. It is difficult for the Ri: What occurred to the mind of the questioner? For perforce he knew that our Mishnah is dealing with [a case] below ten [handbreadths], [even] without the challenge from Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda — for anything above ten [handbreadths in the public domain] is an exempt domain [mekom petor], and everyone agrees that one is not liable [for carrying into it]! And if so, what did he challenge from Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda? For this is an obvious matter: that below ten [handbreadths] it would not be a private domain, as we learned below in [the chapter] HaZorek (below, Shabbat 99a): "The embankment of a cistern or a rock that are ten [handbreadths] high and four wide, one who takes from them or places upon them is liable; [if they are] less than this, he is exempt." And it is obvious that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, was speaking only of [a basket] above ten [handbreadths]!
